label: D2 after choosing a1, when the previous trial reached S2 and was rewarded
explanation: Fires only at D2 and only when the agent just chose a1 (in_action == 1). It never fires at D1 or GO, or after a2. The strongest activations come right after a rewarded a1 -> S2 rare transition on the previous trial: the agent stays on a1, and the top windows usually land in S2 again. The recorded predicate uses only observed variables (D2, a1 chosen, previous trial reached S2 and was rewarded). On dev it has precision 0.87, recall 0.36, F1 0.51 and mass recall 0.64. The rest is a long tail of weak activations (bottom quartiles) at D2 after a1 whenever S2 is involved: either this trial reached S2 via a rare transition, or the previous trial was in S2. The broad version (D2 & a1 & prev_reward == 1 & (in_state == 2 | prev_state == 2)) gets mass recall 0.93 but precision only 0.34. Magnitude is largest when a1 was chosen after a rare-rewarded a1 -> S2 trial. The feature is also more active mid-episode (trials 40-80), when S1 is good, and when the policy logit is near zero. In short, it looks like a conflict signal: a1 chosen while S2 was recently rewarded.
